title: Fine-Tuning the Processes of Steroid Hormone Biosynthesis: SULT2A1/1E1 and CYP21A2 Interaction
content: The high physiological activity of steroid hormones requires multilevel regulation of their biosynthesis. Cytosolic sulfotransferases, specifically SULT2A1 and SULT1E1, convert steroid precursors into mobile sulfated depot forms, diverting them from key steroidogenic cytochromes P450. Given the previously demonstrated CYP17A1–SULT interactions, this study aims to verify the hypothesis that CYP21A2 also interacts with SULTs to co-regulate steroid biosynthesis. Using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensing, in vitro enzymatic activity assays, and in silico molecular modeling, we investigated the interplay between CYP21A2 and SULT2A1/1E1. SPR analysis revealed direct, high-affinity protein–protein interactions in the nanomolar range. Thermodynamic assessments indicated that the CYP21A2–SULT1E1 complex is entropy-driven, contrasting with the enthalpy-driven CYP17A1–SULT1E1 interaction. Enzymatic assays demonstrated reciprocal modulatory effects: CYP21A2 exerted a stimulatory effect on pregnenolone sulfation by SULTs, whereas SULT2A1 moderately inhibited CYP21A2 activity. Molecular modeling of binary complexes predicted structural interfaces and continuous intraprotein channels connecting the enzymes' active sites. These findings suggest that CYP–SULT interactions contribute to the fine-tuning of steroid hormone biosynthesis. We propose that these enzymes participate in a highly organized multiprotein network, acting as metabolic switches that dictate the balance between downstream corticosteroid pathways and structural sequestration into sulfated pools.
